CAUSE: Identical calls get the same worktree name, because the per-call `:occurrence` counter is cut off when the name is built. This is a name collision between concurrent calls in the same run. It is not stale directories from earlier runs.

Evidence (read from the code; I couldn't run anything, since I had no shell tool):
- `scripts/wf_run.py`, `_call_key()` (~line 517) returns `f"{sha256_hex}:{occurrence}"`. The counter in `_occurrences` is what separates byte-identical calls, so it is the only part that differs between them. The hash is 64 hex characters, and the counter comes after it.
- `scripts/wf_run.py`, `_run_attempt()` (~line 818) builds the worktree name as `f"wf-{self.run_id[:24]}-{call_key[:12]}-a{attempt}"`. `call_key[:12]` is the first 12 characters of the digest, so the `:N` suffix is always dropped.
- With the same prompt and options, the digest is the same. `run_id` and `attempt` are also the same, so all 10 calls get the name `wf-<run>-<digest12>-a1`.
- `_prepare_workspace_sync()` calls `app/workspace.py:create_worktree()`. That derives `wt_path = WORKTREE_ROOT/<repo_slug>/<name>` and raises `ValueError("worktree already exists: …")` at line 582 if the path exists (`if wt_path.exists()`).
- At concurrency 3, a second call starts while the first still holds its worktree, so it hits that check. The branch name `feat/<slug>/<name>` collides in the same way. Calls that run one after another would not collide, because the earlier worktree is discarded first. That matches the "10 at concurrency 3" symptom.
- Batches with different prompts have different digests, so they don't collide. The writable workspace option only matters because the worktree is created when `tools == "all"` and `workspace_repo` is set.
- The stale-directory guess doesn't fit. The run directory is fresh, `git worktree list` is empty, and the collision is between sibling calls of the same run.

Reproduction status: I did not run the process, so this is not confirmed by an actual failure. I wrote `scratch/names.py`, which computes `f"wf-RUN-{k[:12]}-a1"` for keys `<digest>:0..2` and should print one name. I didn't execute it. Next step: run that script, then run a batch of 3 identical writable calls and check that it raises the same `ValueError`.

Fix I recommend: put the occurrence into the name, for example by deriving the name from `call_key.replace(":", "-")` with a hash or truncation that keeps the counter (`digest[:12]-o{occurrence}`). Keep `-a{attempt}`. The archive path already uses the full `call_key`, so it doesn't collide. Add a test with 10 identical calls at concurrency 3 to `tests/test_wf_run.py`.
